deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the text of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854, published by Dedekind 1867), §8, the proof of Lehrsatz 1, i.e. Riemann's first lemma. Setting: Omega = sum A_n with A_n = a_n cos nx + b_n sin nx, A_0 = b_0/2. F(x) = C + C'x + A_0 x^2/2 - sum_{n>=1} A_n/n^2 is the twice-integrated series. Claim: if sum A_n converges to f(x), then [F(x+a+b)-F(x+a-b)-F(x-a+b)+F(x-a-b)]/(4ab) -> f(x) as a,b -> 0 with b/a staying finite.

Case b = a (begun on the previous page). Termwise,
 Delta^2F/(4a^2) = sum_{n>=0} A_n c_n, with c_n = (sin(n a)/(n a))^2 and c_0 = 1.
Write S_n = A_0+...+A_{n-1} = f + eps_n, so A_n = eps_{n+1} - eps_n and eps_0 = -f. Given delta, choose m with |eps_n| < delta for n > m, and take a with m a < pi.
Abel summation (implicit step, mine): sum_n (eps_{n+1}-eps_n) c_n = -eps_0 c_0 + sum_{n>=1} eps_n (c_{n-1} - c_n) = f + sum_{n>=1} eps_n (c_{n-1} - c_n). This is legitimate because eps_n is bounded and c_n -> 0.

The remainder is split into three parts.
(1) Indices n = 1..m. This is a finite number of terms. Each factor c_{n-1}-c_n is continuous in a and tends to 0, so the part tends to 0.
(2) Indices n = m+1..s, where s = floor(pi/a). On [0, pi] the function (sin t/t)^2 is decreasing, so c_{n-1}-c_n > 0. The sum telescopes, giving |part 2| < delta (c_m - c_s) <= delta.
(3) Indices n > s. Split
 c_{n-1}-c_n = [sin^2((n-1)a)/((n-1)a)^2 - sin^2((n-1)a)/(n a)^2] + [sin^2((n-1)a) - sin^2(n a)]/(n a)^2.
By sin^2 u - sin^2 v = sin(u+v) sin(u-v), the second bracket equals -sin((2n-1)a) sin(a)/(n a)^2.
Hence |eps_n (c_{n-1}-c_n)| < delta (1/((n-1)a)^2 - 1/(n a)^2) + delta/(n^2 a), using sin a <= a.
Summing over n > s: the first sum telescopes to delta/(s a)^2. The second is (delta/a) sum_{n>s} 1/n^2 < delta/(s a). So |part 3| < delta (1/(s a)^2 + 1/(s a)). Since s a -> pi, this tends to delta (1/pi^2 + 1/pi).

Conclusion: the remainder's limit, strictly its limsup, has absolute value at most delta (1 + 1/pi + 1/pi^2). Since delta is arbitrary, it is 0. Thus Delta^2F(x; 2a)/(4a^2) -> f(x).

General case. Define delta_1 and delta_2 by
 F(x+a+b) - 2F(x) + F(x-a-b) = (a+b)^2 (f + delta_1),
 F(x+a-b) - 2F(x) + F(x-a+b) = (a-b)^2 (f + delta_2).
These are the symmetric case with half-steps (a+b)/2 and (a-b)/2. Subtracting, and using (a+b)^2 - (a-b)^2 = 4ab, gives the mixed difference = 4ab f + (a+b)^2 delta_1 - (a-b)^2 delta_2.
By the special case, delta_1 and delta_2 -> 0. So the error (a+b)^2/(4ab) delta_1 - (a-b)^2/(4ab) delta_2 -> 0 provided these coefficients stay bounded. That holds when b/a stays finite (and bounded away from 0), as concluded on the next page.
errors: 'nähert sich ... einem Grenzwerth' is imprecise: existence of the limit is not shown. Only limsup |remainder| <= delta(1+1/pi+1/pi^2) is proved, which suffices.
The bound for part 3 silently uses |sin((2n-1)a)| <= 1 and sin a <= a.
In part 2, the bound is really delta(c_m - c_s) with c_m <= 1, i.e. <= delta. Later Riemann uses just delta, which is consistent.
In the general case, boundedness of (a+b)^2/(4ab) requires both b/a and a/b to stay bounded. Riemann's 'Verhältniss endlich' must be read as finite and nonzero.
The case a = b makes delta_2 undefined, but there the claim is the special case itself; trivial.

results.what: If sum A_n converges to f(x), the second symmetric difference quotient of the twice-integrated series F converges to f(x). Proved via Abel summation and a three-part splitting of the sum with weights (sin n a/(n a))^2.
results.modern_name: Riemann's first lemma (Riemann summability method R_2 is regular / Schwarz-Riemann second symmetric derivative)

results.what: Reduction of the mixed difference with independent a,b to the symmetric second difference, via (a+b)^2-(a-b)^2=4ab.

deep.surprise_reason: This page is (a manuscript copy of) the proof of Lehrsatz 1 in §8 of Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series, which is famous and fully credited to him.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'von jedem m+1' should read 'von m+1' or 'vom Index m+1'. The published text has '2) von m+1 bis zur grössten unter pi/alpha liegenden ganzen Zahl, welche s sei'.
Notation like sin(n-1)α^2 means sin^2((n-1)α), Riemann's convention.
The bound in part 3 refers to the general term ('dass es', i.e. das allgemeine Glied); the first bracket is (sin(n-1)α/((n-1)α))^2 - (sin(n-1)α/(nα))^2 as transcribed.
'22' and '30.' at top left are archival/page numbers, not mathematical content.
